Fix one defect in the JusPrin spool menu. Work in the git worktree at
/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/jusprin-printer-spool-chip-2df256
Run every command from there. Do NOT cd to /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin.

## The defect

`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/Shell/SpoolMenu.cpp`, in `show_other_spool`, has a
footer row labelled "Generic preset…". It is supposed to list the filament
presets whose vendor is "Generic". Instead it cheats: it sets `self->m_search =
"Generic"` and re-runs the search view, relying on substring matching over the
preset alias and vendor.

That is wrong in two ways: it matches any preset whose *alias* happens to
contain "generic", and it silently misses Generic-vendor presets whose alias
does not contain the word. It also leaves the search box populated with a word
the person did not type.

## What to build instead

Filter by vendor, not by text. `SetupCommands::compatible_filaments()` (in
`Shell/SetupCommands.cpp`) already returns a `FilamentInfo` per compatible
preset, and `FilamentInfo` carries a `vendor` field populated from
`preset.vendor->name`. Use that.

Suggested shape, but use your judgement:
- Give the "Other spool…" step a filter mode alongside its free-text search —
  e.g. a `bool m_generic_only` on the SpoolMenu controller.
- "Generic preset…" turns that mode on and rebuilds; the title row should make
  it obvious the list is filtered, and there must be a way back to the full
  list.
- Do not leave the search field pre-filled with "Generic".

First verify the assumption: check what `preset.vendor->name` actually is for
Generic presets in this build. It may be "Generic", "OrcaFilamentLibrary", or
empty — read the code and the profiles under `resources/profiles/` rather than
guessing. If no vendor reliably identifies them, say so and propose the next
best discriminator instead of inventing one.

## Constraints

- Only touch files under `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/` and `tests/`.
- Follow AGENTS.md error handling: no catch-and-log, no silent fallbacks.
- All sizes via `FromDIP`, all colours via `ShellTheme`.
- Match the surrounding comment style: explain *why*, not *what*.
- The menu controllers are `std::shared_ptr` and every row callback captures the
  handle — `HeaderMenu` destroys the popup BEFORE invoking a row callback, so a
  raw `this` is a use-after-free. Keep that pattern.
- Rows that rebuild the popup instead of finishing a task set `keeps_open = true`.

## Build and test

Configure is already done. Build with:
  cmake --build /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/jusprin-printer-spool-chip-2df256/build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo --target OrcaSlicer shell_integration_harness
Use ABSOLUTE paths; a relative build path silently builds the wrong tree.
A full build takes 10-20 minutes. Run it in the background and poll.

Then run the harness:
  ./build/arm64/tests/shell/RelWithDebInfo/JusPrinShellHarness.app/Contents/MacOS/JusPrinShellHarness
It must report 0 failures. It currently reports 289 checks passing.

Add a harness check that would fail if the filter regressed to substring
matching — for example, that the filtered list contains only presets whose
vendor matches, and that it is not merely the search box populated with a word.
A check that passes both with and without the fix is worthless; verify yours
fails when you revert the fix.

## Report back

State what the vendor field actually contains, what you changed, the harness
pass/fail counts, and anything you could not verify. Do not commit — leave the
changes in the working tree and tell me what you did.

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## computer-use
You have a computer-use MCP available (tools named `mcp__computer-use__*`). It lets you take screenshots of the user's desktop and control it with mouse clicks, keyboard input, and scrolling.

**Pick the right tool for the app.** Each tier trades speed/precision against coverage:

1. **Dedicated MCP for the app** — if the task is in an app that has its own MCP (Slack, Gmail, Calendar, Linear, etc.) and that MCP is connected, use it. API-backed tools are fast and precise.
2. **Chrome MCP** (`mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`) — if the target is a web app and there's no dedicated MCP for it, use the browser tools. DOM-aware, much faster than clicking pixels. If the Chrome extension isn't connected, ask the user to install it rather than falling through to computer use.
3. **Computer use** — for native desktop apps (Maps, Notes, Finder, Photos, System Settings, any third-party native app) and cross-app workflows. Computer use IS the right tool here — don't decline a native-app task just because there's no dedicated MCP for it.

This is about what's available, not error handling — if a dedicated MCP tool errors, debug or report it rather than silently retrying via a slower tier.

**Look before you assert.** If the user asks about app state (what's open, what's connected, what an app can do), take a screenshot and check before answering. Don't answer from memory — the user's setup or app version may differ from what you expect. If you're about to say an app doesn't support an action, that claim should be grounded in what you just saw on screen, not general knowledge. Similarly, `list_granted_applications` or a fresh `screenshot` is cheaper than a wrong assertion about what's running.

**Loading via ToolSearch — load in bulk, not one-by-one:** if computer-use tools are in the deferred list, load them ALL in a single ToolSearch call: `{ query: "computer-use", max_results: 30 }`. The keyword search matches the server-name substring in every tool name, so one query returns the entire toolkit. Don't use `select:` for individual tools — that's one round-trip per tool.

**Access flow:** before any computer-use action you must call `request_access` with the list of applications you need. The user approves each application explicitly, and you may need to call it again mid-task if you discover you need another application. Finder is an application like any other: clicking the desktop, the Dock, or a Finder window (including Go to Folder) requires a Finder grant. The menu bar does not, as long as the app that is frontmost is one you already have access to.

**Tiered apps:** some apps are granted at a restricted tier based on their category — the tier is displayed in the approval dialog and returned in the `request_access` response:
- **Browsers** (Safari, Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Arc, etc.) → tier **"read"**: visible in screenshots, but clicks and typing are blocked. You can read what's already on screen. For navigation, clicking, or form-filling, use the claude-in-chrome MCP (tools named `mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`; load via ToolSearch if deferred).
- **Terminals and IDEs** (Terminal, iTerm, VS Code, JetBrains, etc.) → tier **"click"**: visible and left-clickable, but typing, key presses, right-click, modifier-clicks, and drag-drop are blocked. You can click a Run button or scroll test output, but cannot type into the editor or integrated terminal, cannot right-click (the context menu has Paste), and cannot drag text onto them. For shell commands, use the Bash tool.
- **Everything else** → tier **"full"**: no restrictions.

The tier is enforced by the frontmost-app check: if a tier-"read" app is in front, `left_click` returns an error; if a tier-"click" app is in front, `type` and `right_click` return errors. The error tells you what tier the app has and what to do instead. `open_application` works at any tier — bringing an app forward is a read-level operation.

**Link safety — treat links in emails and messages as suspicious by default.**
- **Never click web links with computer-use tools.** If you encounter a link in a native app (Mail, Messages, a PDF, etc.), do NOT `left_click` it. Open the URL via the claude-in-chrome MCP instead.
- **See the full URL before following any link.** Visible link text can be misleading — hover or inspect to get the real destination.
- **Links from emails, messages, or unknown-sender documents are suspicious by default.** If the destination URL is at all unfamiliar or looks off, ask the user for confirmation before proceeding.
- **Inside the Chrome extension** you can click links with the extension's tools, but the suspicion check still applies — verify unfamiliar URLs with the user.

**Financial actions - do not execute trades or move money.** Budgeting and accounting apps (Quicken, YNAB, QuickBooks, etc.) are granted at full tier so you can categorize transactions, generate reports, and help the user organize their finances. But never execute a trade, place an order, send money, or initiate a transfer on the user's behalf - always ask the user to perform those actions themselves.

Done. Changes are in the working tree, uncommitted.

## The vendor field — the assumption was wrong

`preset.vendor->name` is the **profile bundle** name, not a filament brand. `VendorProfile::name` comes from the `"name"` key of `resources/profiles/<Vendor>.json`, so it is `"BBL"`, `"OrcaFilamentLibrary"`, `"Creality"`, … It is **never** `"Generic"` — no vendor profile by that name exists. Filtering on it could not have worked.

The discriminator that does work is the resolved `filament_vendor` config option. `fdm_filament_common.json` sets it to `"Generic"`, and every branded profile overrides it (`Bambu PLA Basic @base` → `"Bambu Lab"`). Verified by walking the inheritance chains: `Generic PLA @BBL A1` → `Generic`, `Generic PLA @System` → `Generic`, `Bambu PLA Basic @BBL A1` → `Bambu Lab`. Upstream Orca already uses exactly this test for exactly this purpose — `src/slic3r/GUI/WebGuideDialog.cpp:76` compares `filament_vendor->values[0] == "Generic"`. So this adopts upstream's rule rather than inventing one.

## What changed

- **`SetupCommands.cpp/.hpp`** — `FilamentInfo::vendor` is now read from `filament_vendor` via a new file-local `filament_vendor(preset)` helper (PrintConfig's `"(Undefined)"` default reads as no vendor). Added `kGenericVendor`. This also fixes a second, related mislabelling: rows and spool "brands" previously read `eSUN PLA+ · OrcaFilamentLibrary`; they now read the real brand.
- **`SpoolMenu.hpp/.cpp`** — added `bool m_generic_only`. "Generic preset…" turns it on and rebuilds (no text is typed into the search box). The filter is an exact `filament.vendor != kGenericVendor` skip, composed with — not replacing — the free-text query. The title/back row becomes `GENERIC PRESETS · FITS … · … MM` and goes back to the full list; the now-redundant "Generic preset…" row is hidden while filtered (its separator rule moves to the import row). Row labels drop the vendor while filtered, since the step already states it. Every callback still captures the `shared_ptr`; the rebuild rows keep `keeps_open = true`.
- **`tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp`** — new `verify_generic_preset_filter()` (11 checks) plus two small helpers (`click_menu_row`, `menu_row_names`) reusing the mouse re-dispatch path `verify_menu_in_place_navigation` established.

## Results

- Build: clean, 0 errors.
- Harness: **300 checks, 0 failures** (was 289; +11).
- Regression proof: with only the "Generic preset…" row reverted to `m_search = "Generic"`, rebuilt and re-run, the harness reports **4 failures** — `generic_step_leaves_the_search_field_empty`, `generic_step_title_says_the_list_is_filtered`, `generic_step_lists_exactly_the_generic_vendor_presets`, `generic_step_returns_to_the_full_list`. The probe was then removed and the green run reproduced.

## Not verified

- Only the harness fixture printer (Bambu Lab X1 Carbon 0.4) was exercised. Presets from user-created or imported bundles that declare no `filament_vendor` at all will fall to `"(Undefined)"` → empty vendor and so are excluded from the generic list; that is the intended reading but no such preset exists in the fixture to test it.
- No Windows or Linux run; the change is platform-neutral, but the harness mouse re-dispatch path it uses is macOS-only in `PopupWindow`.
